R4E-bear-atv-0004.name: 2.2 km NE of Spillimacheen River
R4E-bear-atv-0004.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R4E-bear-atv-0004.parkWhat: where the truck road ends (TFL14 Cp178); unload the ATV (all terrain vehicle)

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2010 (16 years old), 100 m E: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2015 (fire N20484), 250 m SE: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
S facing slope, 18 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

flags.t: Region 4: it is unlawful to feed or bait deer, elk, moose and other hoofed game, or turkeys, anywhere in the Kootenay Region (synopsis page 37, 99%). Snowmobiles may not be used for hunting in Region 4 from 1 April to 30 November (page 37, 99%).

seasonRows.notes: bag 2; private land only, with landowner permission

plan: Drive: from Village of Radium Hot Springs, about 117 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 51.15361, -117.05447, where the truck road ends (TFL14 Cp178); unload the ATV (all terrain vehicle). Map links below.
Ride: 3.8 km on Sec35, Sec33 by ATV (all terrain vehicle) or 4x4 on rough road, estimate. Then walk 120 m NW, climb about 11 m.

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 4-34, Region 4. No baiting in Region 4. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-01, closures 2026-10-16.
R4E-bear-atv-0004.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 4-34: about 717 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.18 days per square km, middle third of BC MUs; access: average access. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

tags.label: Good for 2
tags.why: Cover edge here (cutblock or burn): one hunter sits at a crossing or glasses, the other walks the edge slowly with the wind at their back toward the stander. Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).

tags.label: Good solo
tags.why: Short pack out: 0.1 km and about 11 m of climb from the parking (Tip). Cell coverage is not in the data: leave a trip plan and carry SOS or a satellite messenger (lesson: Bush safety).

R4E-duck-backcountry-0001.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).

evidence.t: About 5 wetlands within 2 km (estimate): ducks move between them.
Beside Bobbie Burns Creek: backwater or oxbow (estimate).

plan: Drive: from Village of Radium Hot Springs, about 99 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate). Via Hwy 95, Brisco Rd, Bugaboo Creek FSR, Sec 01.
Park: 51.02014, -116.96004, pull off on Main/Spur 5-1 (gravel road). Map links below.
Walk: 5.6 km W, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 1,073 m, about 219 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 100 m S of the spot at 1,550 m (51.03546, -117.03543). Water: Bobbie Burns Creek 60 m NW (estimate).
Hunt: ducks, Sept, Oct, Nov, Dec (season rows). Set up on the shore with the wind at your back: ducks land into the wind (Tip). Shoot only birds you can retrieve.
